plantRole.text: The main cation of the cell sap; drives turgor and stomatal opening and activates many enzymes, without being built into organic molecules.

humanRole.text: The main positive ion inside cells; with sodium it sets the membrane potential of nerves and muscles.

history.nameOrigin: Named by Davy after potash ('pot ashes'), the alkali he electrolysed to obtain it.
history.symbolNote: K comes from the New Latin kalium, from the Arabic al-qali, 'plant ashes'.
history.note: The first metal ever obtained by electrolysis, from molten caustic potash.

prose.text: Potassium is a soft alkali metal that reacts so violently with water that the hydrogen released catches fire, its flame tinted lilac by the potassium. Living things depend on it: plants use potassium to open and close the pores in their leaves, which is why potash is a major fertiliser, and our nerves rely on it too. A small fraction, 0.0117 %, of natural potassium is radioactive potassium-40, with a half-life of about 1.25 billion years, so every human body is faintly radioactive. The nineteenth electron enters 4s rather than 3d, giving [Ar] 4s¹ (ground term ²S₁/₂): the first place in the table where a new shell starts before the one beneath is full.
